title: An immutable config built with defensive copies

blocks.text: The page's `ImmutableConfig` shows how a builder produces an **immutable** object: `final` fields, no setters, and **defensive copies** of the builder's collections, so the product never changes after `build()`, whatever happens to the builder or to the lists callers get back.

Write `ImmutableConfig` with `host()`, `port()`, `ssl()`, `allowedOrigins()` and `properties()`, and its `Builder` (`ImmutableConfig.builder()`) with `host`, `port`, `ssl`, `addOrigin`, `property` and `build()`:

items: Defaults: host `localhost`, port `8080`, ssl `false`, no origins, no properties.
`build()` refuses a port outside `0..65535` with `IllegalStateException`; `port(...)` itself accepts any number, so a later `port(...)` can fix it.
Adding to the builder after `build()` does not change a built config, and the config's own list and map cannot be modified.

cases.says: Unset fields take the defaults localhost, 8080 and no SSL, and chosen values and origins appear in the config.
An origin or property added to the builder after build() does not appear in the config already built.
allowedOrigins() and properties() refuse changes with UnsupportedOperationException.
Ports 0 and 65535 are accepted; -1 and 65536 are refused by build() (not by port()) with IllegalStateException; port(70000).port(443) builds port 443.

concepts: Optional parameters get sensible defaults in the builder.
The product has final fields, no setters, and defensive copies of its collections, so nothing can change it after build().
